name: MongoDB

Software Engineer (junior–mid).dsaDepth: Moderate - practical, non-puzzle coding (arrays/strings/hash-maps/data-processing) via a third-party interviewer, with reasoning-out-loud valued as much as the answer
rounds: Recruiter screen (~30 min): background, stack, motivation, logistics

Technical screen (~60 min, live coding): for junior/mid roles often run via Karat (a third-party interview service); 2-3 practical problems (not puzzle-style) - arrays, strings, hash maps, data processing
Hiring-manager round (~60 min): project depth, decision-making, conflict handling - often gates whether the onsite happens
Onsite loop (several interviews, 1-2 days): further coding, system design, behavioral, and MongoDB/database-specific questions (SQL vs NoSQL trade-offs are a recurring topic, unsurprisingly)
extraTopics: Narrating complexity and trade-offs out loud unprompted - several candidates note that an algorithmically correct answer still felt at risk if the reasoning wasn’t made explicit
Basic database/NoSQL fundamentals given the product domain

Senior Software Engineer (SE3).dsaDepth: Heavy - senior candidates code directly with a MongoDB engineer instead of the third-party screener, and the loop adds LLD/HLD
rounds: Technical screen with an actual MongoDB engineer (not Karat) for senior candidates
Onsite: 2 coding rounds, 1 system design (LLD + HLD), 1 behavioral round
extraTopics: Low-level AND high-level design in the same loop
Bug-bash-style debugging exercises reported in some India pipelines
Senior Software Engineer (SE3).notes: India-based reports (Gurgaon) describe a longer, 5-round loop that candidates found notably tiring.
